newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - CANTV IPO jumps in N.Y. trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - CANTV IPO jumps in N.Y. trade.

text.p: Shares of Venezuelan telephone company CANTV jumped in heavy New York trade on Friday to highlight American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

The initial public offering of most of the Venezuelan government's 49 percent share in the company had 8.5 million shares traded by late morning to lead New York Stock Exchange volume. The shares rose to 26 from an initial pricing of $23 a share.
"We see it as a very positive issue. It looks very good," said a trader who specializes in Latin American stocks. "People are very happy with the way it came out."
Company officials have said they hope to raise between $900 million and $1 billion in the sale, one of the biggest international offerings this year out of Latin America.
More than 80 percent of the CANTV shares are to be sold as ADRs listed on the New York Stock Exchange and in London.
"The significance of selling CANTV shares on the international and Venezuelan markets goes far beyond today's event," CANTV president Gilberto Roosen said in a statement.

"It is a clear sign, both in this country and abroad, that the government of Venezuela is committed to the reforms that will further propel our economy and encourage both domestic and international investment."
Among other ADRs, British mining company RTZ Corp Plc rose 1-3/4 to 67, boosted by strong copper prices and an advance in shares of its Australian affiliate CRA Ltd.
Oil stocks continued their recent advance, helped by rising crude oil prices. Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 2-5/8 to 170-3/4 and Total SA rose 3/8 to 41.
Advancers led decliners by a margin of 253 to 194 among an index of 807 ADRs. By late morning, volume was 23 million shares.
